instruction.hanzi: 读一读，说说这些词语是什么意思。
instruction.english: Read the words and phrases aloud and say what they mean.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 马克，你手里拿着什么？
dialogue.pinyin: Mǎkè, nǐ shǒu li názhe shénme?
dialogue.english: Mark, what's that in your hand?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 铅笔。这是你的铅笔吗？
dialogue.pinyin: Qiānbǐ. Zhè shì nǐ de qiānbǐ ma?
dialogue.english: A pencil. Is this your pencil?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 是我的！我找了一个上午。
dialogue.pinyin: Shì wǒ de! Wǒ zhǎole yí ge shàngwǔ.
dialogue.english: It's mine! I've been looking for it all morning.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 在你的椅子下面找到的。
dialogue.pinyin: Zài nǐ de yǐzi xiàmiàn zhǎodào de.
dialogue.english: I found it under your chair.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 太谢谢你了！
dialogue.pinyin: Tài xièxie nǐ le!
dialogue.english: Thanks so much!

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 不客气。你看，教室的门开着，刘老师来了吗？
dialogue.pinyin: Bú kèqi. Nǐ kàn, jiàoshì de mén kāizhe, Liú lǎoshī láile ma?
dialogue.english: You're welcome. Look, the classroom door is open. Is Professor Liu here?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 来了，她在里面等着我们呢。
dialogue.pinyin: Lái le, tā zài lǐmiàn děngzhe wǒmen ne.
dialogue.english: Yes, she's inside waiting for us.

newWords.english: to hold, to take, to bring
used to indicate a continuing state

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 王明，电脑上这个孩子是谁？
dialogue.pinyin: Wáng Míng, diànnǎo shang zhège háizi shì shéi?
dialogue.english: Wang Ming, who's this child on the computer?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 是小美。那时候她五岁。
dialogue.pinyin: Shì Xiǎoměi. Nà shíhou tā wǔ suì.
dialogue.english: That's Xiaomei. She was five then.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 她笑着看我们，真漂亮！
dialogue.pinyin: Tā xiàozhe kàn wǒmen, zhēn piàoliang!
dialogue.english: She's smiling at us. She's so pretty!

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 现在她十岁了，长高了很多。
dialogue.pinyin: Xiànzài tā shí suì le, zhǎng gāo le hěn duō.
dialogue.english: She's ten now and she's grown a lot taller.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 她还是那么爱笑吗？
dialogue.pinyin: Tā háishi nàme ài xiào ma?
dialogue.english: Does she still smile that much?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 是啊，她每天都笑着去上学。
dialogue.pinyin: Shì a, tā měi tiān dōu xiàozhe qù shàngxué.
dialogue.english: Yes, she goes to school with a smile every day.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 我想见见她！
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng jiànjian tā!
dialogue.english: I'd love to meet her!

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 好啊，星期六她会来我家。
dialogue.pinyin: Hǎo a, xīngqīliù tā huì lái wǒ jiā.
dialogue.english: Sure, she's coming to my place on Saturday.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 请问，学校的宾馆怎么走？
dialogue.pinyin: Qǐngwèn, xuéxiào de bīnguǎn zěnme zǒu?
dialogue.english: Excuse me, how do I get to the university hotel?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 你一直往前走，到第二个路口往右边走。
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ yìzhí wǎng qián zǒu, dào dì-èr ge lùkǒu wǎng yòubian zǒu.
dialogue.english: Go straight ahead, and at the second crossroads turn right.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 第二个路口？离这儿远吗？
dialogue.pinyin: Dì-èr ge lùkǒu? Lí zhèr yuǎn ma?
dialogue.english: The second crossroads? Is it far from here?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 不远，走十分钟就到了。
dialogue.pinyin: Bù yuǎn, zǒu shí fēnzhōng jiù dào le.
dialogue.english: Not far. It's just a ten-minute walk.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 宾馆在路的左边还是右边？
dialogue.pinyin: Bīnguǎn zài lù de zuǒbian háishi yòubian?
dialogue.english: Is the hotel on the left or the right side of the street?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 在左边，宾馆旁边有一个小商店。
dialogue.pinyin: Zài zuǒbian, bīnguǎn pángbiān yǒu yí ge xiǎo shāngdiàn.
dialogue.english: On the left. There's a little shop next to it.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 我知道了，谢谢您！
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ zhīdào le, xièxie nín!
dialogue.english: Got it. Thank you!

title.english: At the entrance of the classroom building

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 刘老师，您手里拿着这么多书！
dialogue.pinyin: Liú lǎoshī, nín shǒu li názhe zhème duō shū!
dialogue.english: Professor Liu, you're carrying so many books!

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 是啊，这些书都是给我们班的。
dialogue.pinyin: Shì a, zhèxiē shū dōu shì gěi wǒmen bān de.
dialogue.english: Yes, these books are all for our class.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 我帮您拿吧。
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ bāng nín ná ba.
dialogue.english: Let me carry them for you.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 谢谢你，马克。你今天不是有考试吗？
dialogue.pinyin: Xièxie nǐ, Mǎkè. Nǐ jīntiān bú shì yǒu kǎoshì ma?
dialogue.english: Thank you, Mark. Don't you have an exam today?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 是，下午三点开始，现在还早呢。
dialogue.pinyin: Shì, xiàwǔ sān diǎn kāishǐ, xiànzài hái zǎo ne.
dialogue.english: I do, but it starts at three this afternoon. It's still early.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 那好，我们一起往教室走吧。
dialogue.pinyin: Nà hǎo, wǒmen yìqǐ wǎng jiàoshì zǒu ba.
dialogue.english: All right, let's walk to the classroom together.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 您看，班里的同学都在门口等着您呢。
dialogue.pinyin: Nín kàn, bān li de tóngxué dōu zài ménkǒu děngzhe nín ne.
dialogue.english: Look, everyone in the class is waiting for you at the door.

explanation.hanzi: "动词＋着"表示一个动作完成以后留下的状态还在继续，比如"门开着""他穿着红衣服"。"V1着＋V2"表示做第二个动作的方式，比如"笑着说""拿着书走"。否定形式是"没（有）＋动词＋着"。
explanation.english: Verb + 着 (zhe) describes a state that continues after an action: 门开着 "the door is (standing) open", 他手里拿着铅笔 "he's holding a pencil". It paints a picture of how things are right now, so it often goes with 呢 at the end. In the pattern V1着 + V2, the first verb tells you the manner of the second: 笑着说 "to say with a smile", 拿着书去教室 "to go to class carrying books". The negative is 没(有) + verb + 着: 门没开着 "the door isn't open".

examples.pinyin: Ānnà shǒu li názhe yì běn shū.

examples.english: Professor Liu said with a smile, "Very good!"

examples.hanzi: 王明穿着一件黑色的衣服。
examples.pinyin: Wáng Míng chuānzhe yí jiàn hēisè de yīfu.
examples.english: Wang Ming is wearing black clothes.

explanation.hanzi: "不是……吗？"是反问句，说话人心里已经有答案，用这个句子来强调，或者表示有点儿奇怪、想让对方想起一件事。意思是"……是这样的"。
explanation.english: 不是……吗? looks like a question, but the speaker already believes the answer is "yes". It means "Isn't it true that...?" and is used to remind someone of something, to stress a point, or to show surprise when things don't match what you expected: 你不是有考试吗? "Don't you have an exam (so why are you here)?" Put 不是 before the part you want to stress and 吗 at the end.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ bú shì xǐhuan chī yú ma?

examples.hanzi: 今天不是星期六吗？你怎么去学校了？
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān bú shì xīngqīliù ma? Nǐ zěnme qù xuéxiào le?
examples.english: Isn't today Saturday? Why did you go to school?

examples.pinyin: Zhè bú shì nǐ de qiānbǐ ma?

examples.hanzi: 他不是我们班的同学吗？
examples.pinyin: Tā bú shì wǒmen bān de tóngxué ma?
examples.english: Isn't he a classmate from our class?

explanation.hanzi: "往＋方向/地方＋动词"表示动作的方向。常用的有"往前走""往左边走""往右边看""往教室走"。问路、指路的时候很常用。
explanation.english: 往 (wǎng) means "towards". Put it before a direction or a place, then add the verb: 往前走 "walk forward", 往右边走 "go to the right", 往外面看 "look outside", 往教室走 "head towards the classroom". It's the key word for asking and giving directions, often together with 一直 "straight on" and 到……路口 "at the ... crossroads".

prompt.hanzi: 两人一组，分角色读课文。
prompt.english: In pairs, read the dialogues aloud, taking one role each.
Fill in the blanks with 着, 往, 一直, 拿 or 笑.

items.english: Keep going straight and you'll reach the hotel.
Turn right at the second crossroads.
Xiaomei said with a smile, "I'm ten!"

prompt.hanzi: 根据你的情况回答问题。

items.pinyin: Nǐmen bān yǒu duōshao ge xuésheng?
items.english: How many students are in your class?

items.hanzi: 你今天穿着什么颜色的衣服？
items.pinyin: Nǐ jīntiān chuānzhe shénme yánsè de yīfu?
items.english: What color are you wearing today?

items.pinyin: Cóng nǐ jiā qù xuéxiào, zěnme zǒu?
items.english: How do you get from your home to school?

prompt.english: Match each question with a suitable answer.

items.hanzi: 你不是喜欢喝咖啡吗？ — 是，今天我想喝茶。
items.pinyin: Nǐ bú shì xǐhuan hē kāfēi ma? — Shì, jīntiān wǒ xiǎng hē chá.
items.english: Don't you like coffee? — I do, but today I feel like tea.

items.hanzi: 请问，宾馆怎么走？ — 一直往前走，就在路口旁边。
items.pinyin: Qǐngwèn, bīnguǎn zěnme zǒu? — Yìzhí wǎng qián zǒu, jiù zài lùkǒu pángbiān.
items.english: Excuse me, how do I get to the hotel? — Go straight on. It's right by the crossroads.

items.hanzi: 你怎么笑了？ — 小美说的话太好笑了。
items.pinyin: Nǐ zěnme xiào le? — Xiǎoměi shuō de huà tài hǎoxiào le.
items.english: What are you laughing at? — What Xiaomei said was so funny.

items.hanzi: 刘老师在吗？ — 在，她在教室里等着你呢。
items.pinyin: Liú lǎoshī zài ma? — Zài, tā zài jiàoshì li děngzhe nǐ ne.
items.english: Is Professor Liu here? — Yes, she's waiting for you in the classroom.

singleComponentChars.etymology: Originally a drawing of an open hand: the long hooked stroke is the arm and the short strokes across it are the spread fingers. On the left side of a character it shrinks to 扌, as in 打 and 找.

radicals.english: axe (originally a hand axe; now also a unit of weight)
examples: 所 suǒ (place; as in 所以)

radicals.english: head (originally a drawing of a head; related to the head and face)

prompt.hanzi: 两人一组，问路、指路，说说别人在做什么。
prompt.english: In pairs, ask for and give directions, and describe what people are doing.

activities: Draw a simple map of the streets around your school with a hotel, a shop, a restaurant and a hospital. A asks 请问，……怎么走？ and B answers with 一直往前走 / 到第……个路口往左边（右边）走.
Look around the room and describe five things with 着: 门开着, 他手里拿着……, 她穿着…… Your partner guesses who or what you mean.
Remind your partner of things with 不是……吗？: 你不是喜欢……吗？ / 今天不是……吗？ Your partner explains why plans have changed.
Show a photo of yourself or a family member as a child and say how they've changed: 那时候……岁，现在长高了很多。
